newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH METRO SUFFERS SECOND FIRE THIS WEEK - CTK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH METRO SUFFERS SECOND FIRE THIS WEEK - CTK.

text.p: Prague's underground railway network, the Metro, suffered its second fire in a week early on Friday morning but no one was seriously hurt, the Czech news agency CTK reported.
CTK said two Metro workers had been hospitalised and were awaiting the results of blood tests after inhaling smoke in the tunnel.

The fire was a virtual repeat performance of Monday's blaze which happened on the same line, the A line. Both incidents are believed to have been caused by faults in high voltage electrical cables but neither resulted in serious injuries.
Friday's fire started at the Zelivskeho station at 4.10 am (0210 GMT), about two hours before rush hour, CTK said, and services were suspended for two and a half hours.

Line A is the second oldest of the three lines on the electrically-driven Prague system, which was largely built by the communists using Soviet-made trains. The system has largely enjoyed a reputation as safe and efficient.
